outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making a poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or facing the performance impacts of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation occurs when workload demands exceed capacity, representing a common cause of failure in on-premises workloads. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
Cloud computing allows organizations to monitor demand and automate resource adjustments, avoiding over- or under-provisioning. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
outcomes.modelOutput: {"status":"ANSWERED","claims":[{"text":"Making a poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or facing the performance impacts of limited capacity.","ref":"r1c2","quote":"If you make a poor capacity decision when deploying a workload, you might end up sitting on expensive idle resources or dealing with the performance implications of limited capacity."},{"text":"Resource saturation occurs when workload demands exceed capacity, representing a common cause of failure in on-premises workloads.","ref":"r1c1","quote":"A common cause of failure in on-premises workloads is resource saturation, when the demands placed on a workload exceed the capacity of that workload"},{"text":"Cloud computing allows organizations to monitor demand and automate resource adjustments, avoiding over- or under-provisioning.","ref":"r1c1","quote":"In the cloud, you can monitor demand and workload utilization, and automate the addition or removal of resources to maintain the optimal level to satisfy demand without over- or under-provisioning."}]}

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way doors are reversible decisions that can use a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way doors are hard or impossible to reverse and demand additional inspection before they are made. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a cloud service that offers a consistent process to review and measure your architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool is provided by AWS to review workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS WA Tool provides recommendations designed to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool assists in reviewing your approach prior to development, evaluating workloads before production, and checking their state in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
With the tool, workloads can be compared to current AWS architectural best practices to monitor overall status and identify potential risks. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) represents the maximum acceptable delay between a service interruption and the restoration of that service. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 680]
This objective determines the time window considered acceptable for a service to remain unavailable and is established by the organization. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
RTO serves as a target or maximum allowed value for a single availability-impacting event, measuring the time between the start of an outage and the recovery of the workload. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Adding exponential backoff with jitter to client retries allows servers to recover when failures stem from resource overload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Exponential backoff retries requests after progressively longer intervals to lessen the load escalation created by retries. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter introduces randomness to retry intervals to avoid aligning requests into traffic spikes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
A maximum number of retries or elapsed time should be configured to prevent backlogs that lead to metastable failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should be implemented at only one layer of the application stack to avoid compounding retry attempts into a retry storm. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Being aware of service quotas and constraints helps customers prevent service degradation or disruption in their AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Monitoring and automatically managing service quotas and resource constraints can proactively reduce failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
If a constraint is reached unexpectedly, an account's applications or services can experience degradation or disruption. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
Automation can be triggered when a threshold is breached by monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs) of a workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
KPIs should measure business value rather than technical operational aspects of the service. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Monitoring KPIs enables automatic notification and tracking of failures, as well as recovery processes that bypass or fix the failure. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Advanced automation makes it possible to predict and resolve failures before they occur. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
AWS is responsible for protecting the infrastructure that runs all of the services offered in the AWS Cloud, encompassing the hardware, software, networking, and facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS operates, manages, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of the facilities where the service operates. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
The customer is responsible for the guest operating system, including updates and security patches, other associated application software, and configuring the AWS-provided security group firewall. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customer responsibility is determined by the specific AWS Cloud services selected, which dictates the amount of required configuration work. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS secures the underlying cloud infrastructure, whereas customers are responsible for securing their applications, data, and the services they use. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 130]

outcomes.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
outcomes.answer:
Secrets management is best approached by following the guidance to remove, replace, and rotate. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]
Credentials that are no longer necessary for the workload's functioning can be safely removed. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]
Long-term credentials that are still needed can be replaced with temporary or short-term credentials, such as replacing hard-coded access keys with IAM roles. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]
Long-lived secrets that cannot be removed or replaced can be centrally stored, managed, and rotated on a regular basis using a service such as AWS Secrets Manager. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 300]
For application and database credentials, automated rotation should be established and credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
Separation of concerns allows credential rotation to be carried out by a separate component segregated from the rest of the architecture, enabling central rotation. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be allowed to perform the smallest set of actions required to carry out a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle balances usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Operating under the principle of least privilege helps limit unintended access and track who has access to which resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
Workloads should be designed to be scalable and loosely coupled so components can be updated regularly, allowing for frequent, small, and reversible changes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Pairing automated deployment techniques with smaller, incremental changes lowers the blast radius and enables faster reversal during failures. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Implementing automated deployment and delivery services increases the flow of beneficial changes into production by automating repetitive processes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 10]
Teams should make informed deployment decisions by maintaining processes for both successful and unsuccessful changes to their workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]
Before deploying changes, organizations should evaluate their benefits and risks and verify compliance with governance. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
Runbooks are documented processes used to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
In cloud operations, runbooks are used to reduce risk and achieve desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are used to achieve consistent outcomes across different users for activities ranging from onboarding a new team member to deploying a major release. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are often used for routine activities. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Runbooks remain useful for conducting game days and satisfying stringent reporting and auditing requirements. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Documenting procedures in runbooks is used to deliver consistent and prompt responses to well-understood events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.question: How can feature flags and A/B testing be used to experiment safely?
outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be used to safely conduct experiments and gather feedback from users. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
AWS AppConfig Feature Flags provides functionality to create feature flags. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
AWS Lambda versions can be utilized to deploy new function versions for beta testing. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
Feature-flag testing permits flagging individual new features on and off externally from the application so each feature can be validated separately. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]
A/B testing is applied to compare outcomes with the current version across two user testing groups. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier for your team by delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Instead of having an IT team learn to host and run a new technology, organizations should consider consuming that technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Technologies such as NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning require specialized expertise. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
In the cloud, these technologies become consumable services, enabling teams to focus on product development instead of resource provisioning and management. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: What is mechanical sympathy?
outcomes.answer:
Mechanical sympathy involves understanding how cloud services are consumed and always choosing the technology approach that aligns with your workload goals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]
An example of mechanical sympathy is considering data access patterns when selecting a database or storage approach for a workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
AWS Lambda allows failed transactions to be routed to a dedicated Amazon SQS dead-letter queue on a per-function basis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Within AWS Lambda, Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure can be configured to control retries and send metadata from poison-pill messages to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Step Functions should be used whenever possible to minimize custom try/catch, back-off, and retry logic, including saving failed state runs and their state into a DLQ. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: Why should each microservice have its own data persistence layer?
outcomes.answer: In a microservices approach, a central database would prevent the goal of creating decentralized and independent components. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 18]

outcomes.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
outcomes.answer:

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer:
Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources consumed, and increasing or decreasing usage based on business requirements. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]
For instance, development and test environments can be stopped when not in use to achieve potential cost savings of 75%. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]

outcomes.question: Why does the choice of AWS Region matter for the carbon footprint of a workload?
outcomes.answer:
The choice of Region for a workload significantly affects key performance indicators, including performance, cost, and carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]
Placing a workload near Amazon renewable energy projects or in Regions with low published carbon intensity can help reduce its carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]
Regions can be selected based on grid carbon intensity that is lower compared to other locations. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]

outcomes.question: What is the shared responsibility model for sustainability?
outcomes.answer:
Environmental sustainability is shared between customers and AWS. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
AWS bears responsibility for optimizing the sustainability of the cloud by providing efficient, shared infrastructure, water stewardship, and sourcing renewable power. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
Customers bear responsibility for sustainability in the cloud by optimizing workloads and resource utilization, as well as minimizing total resources needed for their workloads. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]

outcomes.question: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery do?
outcomes.answer:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server-hosted applications and server-hosted databases from any source into AWS using block-level replication of the underlying server. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It allows you to use an AWS Cloud Region as a disaster recovery target for workloads hosted on-premises or on another cloud provider. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It can also provide disaster recovery for AWS-hosted workloads consisting only of applications and databases hosted on EC2 rather than RDS. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
The service coordinates and orchestrates the recovery of compute resources when initiated during a drill or failover. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
It replicates data from a primary region to a recovery Region using continual data protection, achieving an RPO measured in seconds and an RTO measured in minutes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
